statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 11, low, for the 04:00Z hour, up from 7. Nasdaq-100 futures are 29,272.75, down 115.00 points and 0.39%, at 04:02Z, holding about 11 points above a fresh overnight low of 29,261.25 after the 29,301 shelf gave way. That marginal low break and the position near the extreme are the reason Tail rises, but the whole 219-point overnight band spans only 0.75% and both edges were faded earlier in the session, which is not the persistent no-retracement path Tail measures. S&P 500 futures are 0.09% lower and the Dow contract is near flat, so the drag stays Nasdaq-specific, consistent with Alibaba's $10.2 billion Hong Kong placement to fund AI capital spending sending its shares down as much as 10% and with a soft semiconductor tone. Stress is 40, moderate, up from 38: the 30-year yield sits near 5.276%, close to a 19-year peak, and the Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions is scheduled for 18:00Z. Offsetting that, VIX finished Friday at 14.89, down 6.00%, WTI is near $85.62 and Brent near $92.99 on pre-announcement profit-taking, gold is near $4,623 and Treasury futures are modestly bid. Confidence is 85, high. The danger window remains 18:00Z-20:00Z.
recommendation: The overnight path has tilted lower without becoming a trend. Nasdaq-100 futures printed 29,480.25, rotated twice through a 29,301-29,470 band, then extended marginally to a new low of 29,261.25 and are 29,272.75 at 04:02Z. Holding within a dozen points of the session low is a genuine Tail amplifier and lifts the reading from 7 to 11, but it is the only amplifier present: the break is roughly 40 points deep, the full band spans 0.75%, and there is no sequence of shallow pullbacks or repeated extension after failed retracements. Cross-asset evidence conflicts rather than confirms. S&P 500 futures are 0.09% lower and Dow futures are near flat, VIX is below 15, Treasury futures are bid, gold is higher near $4,623 and crude is roughly 1.5% lower on profit-taking before the sanctions announcement. The Nasdaq-specific character fits the Alibaba AI-capex placement and a soft semiconductor tone rather than an index-level risk-off impulse, and Asian equity losses of 0.3-0.8% are contained. The identifiable risks ahead are scheduled rather than observed. Treasury Secretary Bessent's news conference on new Iran sanctions at 18:00Z, confirmed as 2 p.m. EDT, is the one credible geopolitical discontinuity of the day, and the danger window is held narrow at 18:00Z-20:00Z rather than extended across the session; conditional Tail peaks at 19 there, still below the block threshold, because event importance and surprise magnitude raise Stress before they establish a pathological price path. Nvidia's results on 26 August and Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole on 28 August sit outside this horizon but damp conviction inside it. The structure that would change this assessment is specific: an opening auction that extends with shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after a failed retracement, NQ holding a session extreme while yields, VIX, oil, semiconductors and breadth align in the same direction, or a sanctions announcement that produces a delayed second leg rather than orderly repricing.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures set a marginal overnight low near 29,261 in a 0.75% band; Tail 11, low, mapped state EA_ON
body: Nasdaq-100 futures are 29,272.75 at 04:02Z, 115.00 points and 0.39% lower, having extended the overnight low to 29,261.25 from the 29,301 shelf that held twice earlier in the session. Price is holding near that low, which is why Tail moves up from 7 to 11, but the break is shallow and the 219-point band spans only 0.75% of index value. The weakness is index-specific: S&P 500 futures are 0.09% lower at 7,684.00 in a 21.75-point range, and Dow futures are near flat. Alibaba priced a HK$80 billion, $10.2 billion placement of new shares at HK$112.70 to fund AI infrastructure, an 8.4% discount that sent the Hong Kong line down as much as 10% and put AI capital-spending dilution back in focus days before Nvidia reports. Latest-session semiconductor tone was soft, with the semiconductor industry group 0.31% lower and ARM and Intel down 2.95% and 2.24%, while megacap performance was split. Cross-asset evidence does not align with equity weakness. VIX closed Friday at 14.89, down 6.00%, in a 14.77-15.95 range. H.15 for 20 August shows the 2-year at 4.19% and the 10-year at 4.69%, with the 30-year near 5.276% and close to a 19-year peak, and Treasury futures are modestly bid overnight. WTI is near $85.62, down 1.65%, and Brent near $92.99, down 1.49%, as investors take profits before the sanctions announcement after both contracts gained more than 5% last week. Gold is near $4,623, up about 0.4%. Asian equities are mixed to modestly lower, with the Nikkei 0.31% lower, Korea down 0.8%, Taiwan down 0.5% and MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan down 0.2%. Scheduled catalysts dominate the forward path: the Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30Z, the US cash open at 13:30Z, and Treasury Secretary Bessent's news conference on new Iran sanctions at 18:00Z, which anchors the 18:00Z-20:00Z danger window. Delayed cross-asset context collected at 03:40Z was consistent with these primary readings and was used only as confirmation, not as live price-path evidence.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the published Claude Tail reading stayed in a 4-15 band and the mapped policy state was EA_ON in every hour with an assessment. Four hours, 07:00Z and 10:00Z to 12:00Z on 23 August, have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Through the weekend session Tail held at 4 while Stress climbed steadily from 34 to 45 as the Iran sanctions announcement approached. Tail then rose to 15 at 22:00Z on the Globex reopen and eased back through 9, 8, 7 and 9 to 7 as the overnight band was rotated in both directions. Dominant mode was recorded as normal in every available hour.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook keeps Tail in an 9-19 band and the mapped policy state at EA_ON throughout, with the danger window held narrow at 18:00Z-20:00Z. Conditional Tail eases to 10 through the remaining Asian hours, holds near 11 across the European open and morning, then lifts to 15-17 into the 13:30Z US cash open where an opening auction that extends with shallow pullbacks is the structure to watch. It peaks at 19, still below the block threshold, for the two hours covering Treasury Secretary Bessent's 18:00Z news conference on new Iran sanctions and the delayed second-leg risk that overlaps the US power hour, with Stress rising to 52 there. Tail then declines through 14 at the close to 9 in the following Asian session on the assumption that the announcement is absorbed with orderly price discovery. Dominant mode is normal outside the US session, mixed around the open and into pre-event positioning, and event/whipsaw for the two danger-window hours. Every forward value is conditional risk, not observed structure.
